I disagreed pretty much 100%. I really didn't get that into Skyrim because the playstyle just felt stilted and wonky compared to more deliberate systems like WoW and snappier immediate combat such as FPS games utilize. The only thing that kept me returning to ESO at all was the story. It creates real moral dilemma and tension better than any other game I have ever played. There were many really good examples of NPCs doing terrible things to survive, save their farm, aid a family member, or avenge a wrong, and being tasked with judging them, choosing to kill them or turn them in for justice literally made my throat tight because I could so easily see myself reacting the same way.

You want to use pen and paper as a standard of comparison? That's really weird, because what the writing reminds me of more than anything are the great writers who breathed life into the interconnected D&D universe and made it more than a bunch of dice juggling rules lawyers. Anyone who has sympathized with Artemis Entreri, Daru ib Shamiq, Queen Aural, Lord Soth, Raistlin Majere and Kitiara will know immediately what I'm talking about. You know they are evil, or have done things they must be punished for, but everything leading to their fall from grace is easy to look at and say "Yes, I'd likely react that way as well." It's what makes them more than black and white, more than the simple walking loot sacks you lament them not being.

As for the prophet, how short a time did you play that the five levels appearances got on your nerves so badly? From 20 onward it takes so long between levels that when the prophet does spring up it seems fairly organic, because it's usually been a while since you have seen him. Even if you are being carried by far advanced friends and seeing him more than once in a weekend of playing, it's not like he buzzes around like Navi going "Hey, listen!." You can go immediately, or continue to level organically in the world questing and dungeoneering. Sure, he probably could be redone to just spill everything up front instead of "Doling out the story" as you put it and you could wind up beating the main storyline at level 5 without ever experiencing the huge, interesting world going on around it just like you can in Skyrim, but ye gods what a waste that would be.

I'm sure that somewhere amongst it all, ESO really can create meaningful moral dilemmas when looked at in the right light. What I'm saying is I simply didn't find ESO to be a very convincing vehicle for those dilemmas, furthermore not because ESO was badly designed, but because of the designs it applied from other genres.

Also, tying main quest progress to character level is inherently dumb.

I've seen about a dozen of these threads today. "Oh no, Voat is becoming Reddit! People are downvoating things they disagree with instead of just low quality things like they're supposed to, how awful!" News flash, this doesn't only happen on Reddit. It happens on literally any site that uses an upvote/downvote system of organizing things. People are always going to downvote things they don't like. It's human nature, and it's never going to be any different.

Furthermore, it would be downright dumb not to do so. If you are the sort who likes to take moral high grounds and would never ever downvoat something just because you disagree with it, all you're doing is giving your ideological opponents a 2-to-1 advantage over you in the voting system. It's like going into a battle armed with swords against opponents who have crossbows because the Pope told you that crossbows are the Devil's weapon. Maybe the Pope is right and crossbows aren't so great for humanity, but that doesn't change the fact that they exist, your opponents have them, and you're being a buffoon and intentionally putting yourself at a disadvantage.

Also, a lot of people are bashing Atko for removing the 100 CCP requirement to downvote, while remaning completely ignorant of why he did it. People who were willing to cheat the system would go to certain subs and beg for downvotes and get hundreds of them overnight, and Atko, knowing this, was just evening the playing field for people who wanted to play fair. You guys who are complaining about this are like gun control nuts who want guns taken away from law abiding citizens so that they can be better preyed upon by people willing to break the rules.

So, you might ask, why not just do away with downvotes entirely and use only upvotes? While that's certainly a possibility, I for one value the positive two-dimensionality that downvotes bring over the negative hurt feefees they cause when you get them. And if you think that doing away with downvotes will deter vote manipulators, don't kid yourself. They will just upvote the things they want to be seen, and you'll be powerless to downvote them in protest. So, it doesn't solve anything to get rid of downvotes, and everyone seems to like them well enough, considering that an upvote-downvote system has come to be the most widely used one on the internet. So lets keep them, and learn to accept the world for how it actually works instead of how we'd like it to.

Tl;dr- Vote wars are going to happen no matter what, the only solution is getting rid of voting entirely, and fuck that. So get over it.
The voting system should be left the way it is, and everyone should quit bitching about people using downvoats on things they disagree with.
